item.title: The Equational Theory of Rational String-to-String Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.34324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a sound and complete equational axiomatisation of the rational string-to-string functions, which can be seen as a transducer counterpart of the classical axiomatisations of regular languages by Salomaa [JACM'66], Krob [TCS'91], Bloom and \'Esik [MSCS'93], and Kozen [IC'94]. The axioms are stated over a compositional, algebraic syntax for rational functions, namely the rational fragment of the syntax for regular functions introduced by Boja\'nczyk, Daviaud and Krishna [LICS'18]. The axiomatisation is finitary, as it consists of finitely many uniform families of axioms, each parameterised by the types involved. It is also purely equational: it consists only of equations, with no implication rules.
item.dc:creator: Miko{\l}aj Boja\'nczyk, Kacper Lewandowski, Katzper Michno

item.title: Product-Linear POSIX Parsing
item.description: arXiv:2611.34904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: POSIX regular-expression matching reports capture spans determined by the parse tree that its disambiguation rules select. Thompson's classical construction decides whether an expression $E$ matches a text $w$ in product-linear time, $O(|E|\,|w|)$. Whether the POSIX parse can also be computed in product-linear time has remained open since the rules were standardized in 1992. For instance, the algorithm of Okui and Suzuki takes $O(|E|^2|w|)$ time after precomputation. We give, to our knowledge, the first algorithm that computes the POSIX parse and all capture spans in product-linear total time, $O(|E|\,|w|)$. It uses $O(|E|+|w|)$ working space and supports full matching, longest-prefix matching, and leftmost-longest search. The algorithm scans the text backward and keeps one preferred continuation per traversal state. It implements POSIX selection with lists of end positions of the open subexpressions, which it compares and updates in constant time.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Uezato

item.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
item.description: arXiv:2611.33838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the B\"uchi language forgets. Machines sharing their B\"uchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its B\"uchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and B\"uchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.
item.dc:creator: Kenan Oggad
